newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean Metals - Market nervous over LG Metals talk.
newsitem.headline: Korean Metals - Market nervous over LG Metals talk.

text.p: The South Korean base metals market was very nervous in lacklustre trading this week on rumours that leading producer LG Metals Corp was in trouble on the London market and as its stock underwent a rollercoaster ride, traders said on Friday.

LG Metals' stock price surged on Friday virtually recovering all the previous day's losses as the market was heartened by the company's denial on Thursday that it had made any losses in metals futures trading last year, although in did not comment on current trading positions.

Domestic aluminium prices have risen to 1,450,000 won a tonne in line with the LME trend and the won's fall, compared with 1,430,000 won a week ago, while copper prices have risen to 2,286,000 won a tonne from 2,101,000 won a week earlier.
Zinc and lead also remained unchanged at 1,020,000 won a tonne and 706,000 won respectively.
Traders said most local metal importers are incurring heavy losses due to the won's recent steep decline against the dollar.

Early on Friday, the won hit a new 83-month low of 866.00 against the dollar on strong dollar demand affected by the U.S. unit's strength against the yen and the foreign exchange market's view that the dollar is still undervalued, dealers said.
"The dollar's strength against the Japanese yen in world markets is pushing the won lower," a dealer said.
He expected the won to continue to drop due to South Korea's growing trade deficit.

South Korea's customs-cleared trade deficit during the first 29 days of January was estimated at $4.1 billion, the biggest monthly figure ever, compared with a shortfall of $2.13 billion for the whole of January 1996.
Exports were hampered by strikes that hit the nation's auto industry and falling semiconductor prices.
Labour unrest in protest at the passage of a controversial labour law had crippled much of South Korean industry between December 26 and January 18.
In 1996, South Korea's trade deficit totalled a record $20.38 billion, against a $10.06 billion shortfall in 1995, traders said.
